title: Khan Raza v. State of U.P. — restoration on first 6.14 installment
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
disposition: Writ disposed; 6.14 representation; restoration on first installment.
headnote: Writ challenging a recovery citation for electricity arrears of Rs.3,13,417 was disposed of without examining merits. The High Court directed the consumer to represent under clause 6.14 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005 for easy installments, and ordered that the connection be restored on deposit of the first installment as fixed by the licensee, subject to timely payment of remaining installments.
facts: Khan Raza filed a writ seeking to quash a recovery citation dated 15 October 2020 (S.N. DG64561082700, R.C. PRAPTRA-36) issued by respondent no. 3 and to restrain coercive action. He offered to deposit outstanding electricity dues of Rs.3,13,417 in easy installments. Counsel for respondent no. 2 submitted that the installment request could be considered and decided under clause 6.14 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, and asked that reasonable time be allowed.

holding_units.topic: installment facility and restoration on first installment
holding_units.holding: Without examining the merits of the recovery citation, the Court disposed of the writ by directing the petitioner to represent all grievances to the licensee within three weeks for consideration and decision strictly in accordance with law, preferably within four weeks, under clause 6.14. On deposit of the first installment as may be fixed by the licensee, the electricity connection shall be restored, subject to payment of further installments within the period fixed; default disentitles the petitioner to the benefit of the order.

principle_tags.application: A request to pay electricity arrears in easy installments is to be considered by the licensee under clause 6.14; the Court directed restoration of supply on deposit of the first installment as so fixed.

not_decided.point: Validity of the recovery citation dated 15.10.2020
not_decided.note: Writ disposed of without examining merits; the citation was neither quashed nor upheld.
